newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma moves Buddhist relic to Mandalay.
newsitem.headline: Burma moves Buddhist relic to Mandalay.

text.p: A Buddhist relic which escaped damage during a December 25 bombing that killed five people and wounded 17 was moved to Mandalay on Thursday, four days later than originally scheduled.
A source in Burma's Ministry of Religious Affairs said on Thursday the Sacred Tooth Relic, believed to be a tooth of the Lord Buddha, was flown to Burma's second city of Mandalay on Thursday morning.

The relic is on loan from China for 90 days and was originally due to be moved to Mandalay last Sunday. But that plan was changed after the bomb attack in the Kaba Aye Maha Pasana Cave where the relci was housed in Rangoon, the Religious Affairs source said.

Before the change in plans, the relic was to have been sent by road to Mandalay, with one-night stopovers in each of six towns. After four weeks, a similar trip was to be made with stops in six different cities.
Thousands of pilgrims were paying homage at the cave on the outskirts of Rangoon on Christmas Day when two bombs went off.
Burma's military government blamed exiled students and the rebel Karen National Union ethnic group for the bombings. Both groups denied involvement.
